newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nine in 10 HK students lack confidence in China rule.
newsitem.headline: Nine in 10 HK students lack confidence in China rule.

text.p: Nine in 10 students in Hong Kong believe China will not allow the territory a free hand to run its own affairs after Britain pulls out on July 1, an opinion poll indicated on Thursday.

The poll by the Hong Kong City University found 90.4 percent of 470 students in seven Hong Kong universities did not believe Hong Kong people would have a high degree of autonomy as promised by China in its 1984 handover treaty with Britain.
A meagre 0.2 percent said they were confident.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
China has pledged the territory of 6.4 million will enjoy considerable autonomy and keep its capitalist way of life for 50 years after the sovereignty transfer.
The poll also found that 78 percent of students were pessimistic about human rights protection under the Chinese flag, compared with a bare 0.5 percent who were confident.
Jittery Hong Kong has been unnerved by Beijing's recent plan to curb civil and political liberties, and replace the current elected legislature with an appointed body.

The popularity of post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa has fallen recently since his office launched a plan to curb the right to protest and ban foreign funding of political groups after the colony's handover.
